name: NJ-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Chris Smith's long incumbency running for reelection
Democratic challenger minimally funded ($34K raised, $5K on hand)
model.rationale: The district's R+14 lean, Smith's entrenched incumbency, and his large financial advantage over an underfunded challenger all point to a comfortable Republican win, and markets agree at roughly 96-4. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, this stays Safe R.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending or an unexpectedly strong national Democratic environment could narrow the margin, though not realistically the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Chris Smith, one of the longest-serving House members, seeks another term in a New Jersey district that leans Republican by about fourteen points. He enters the general election with roughly $488,000 on hand after raising nearly $600,000, while Democrat Rachel Peace has raised about $34,000 with only $5,000 available. No independent polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Smith about a 96 percent chance of winning.

The fundamentals strongly favor the incumbent: the district's partisan lean, Smith's incumbency advantage, and his financial edge all point the same direction. The Democratic challenger faces steep odds without the resources or name recognition to change the race's trajectory.
